title: Splunk Core User
description: Search with SPL, investigate suspicious activity and Windows event IDs, build dashboards, and write clear evidence-based incident reports using fictional datasets.
baseline: Splunk Enterprise 10.4+ · supported Windows Server guest · lab.example.test dummy data · SPL (not SPL2)
prerequisite: Before you start, have a supported Windows Server practice VM ready in VMware Workstation Pro, an administrator account for setup, and an eligible Splunk Enterprise trial or license. supplies: A supported x86-64 Windows Server guest called SPLUNK01, with resources checked against the selected release’s official requirements.
An official Splunk Enterprise installer and a trial/license that permits scheduling; a website visit does not create an entitlement.
The supplied 12-event cloudseam-web.csv and three-row cloudseam-status.csv files. All names and events are fictional.
A private browser session on the guest at http://localhost:8000 after installation. No paid Azure resources are needed.
The supplied 16-event cloudseam-security.csv for injection-pattern and external-login investigations. No attacks are sent; you analyze prepared logs.
The supplied 14-event cloudseam-windows-events.csv and incident report template for Windows investigations.

steps.title: Find the SQL-like patterns
steps.where: Your practice VM → browser → http://localhost:8000 → Search & Reporting
actions: Replace the Search bar with the query below. Run it with All time, then open Statistics.
Look for UNION SELECT and OR 1=1 in decoded_request. You should see three events from 203.0.113.50.
